verdict.rationale: Obsidian documents a first-party headless Sync client that syncs vaults without the desktop app and is explicitly positioned for CI pipelines, agents, and automated workflows (obsidian-docs-10). That headless mode covers only vault syncing; there is no evidence the core app itself (plugins, Bases, templates, publish) can run headlessly. The URI protocol needs the desktop app, and editing plain-text files with external tools is a user workaround, so neither earns credit. Missing for 10: headless or CLI operation of the app's core functionality beyond sync, detailed docs on CI setup, and independent hands-on corroboration of the headless client.
